chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Three breaths are better than one breath (whilst drinking).

key_terms.أَفْضَل: Better, superior, more virtuous — comparative form indicating preference in Islamic law and ethics
key_terms.أَنْفَاس: Plural of nafas (breath/sip); refers to the pauses taken between drinking rather than inhaling

ai.seo_question: Is it sunnah to drink water in three sips or three breaths?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recommends taking three separate breaths when drinking, rather than drinking in one continuous breath. This guidance reflects Islamic etiquette (adab) of eating and drinking, rooted in the Prophetic tradition of moderation and mindfulness. The teaching encourages pausing between sips, which is considered both physically healthier and spiritually more mindful.
